title: Backend: DELETE /api/v1/organisations/:org_id/groups/:group_id deletes any organisation's group because the caller is never checked
description:
## Summary

`DELETE /api/v1/organisations/:org_id/groups/:group_id` has no authorisation beyond a valid bearer token. The controller never reads `userClaims`, and the service only checks that the organisation exists before deleting the group with the two path parameters. Any authenticated user can therefore delete any group in any organisation by sending that organisation's id and the group id.

`Group.Channels` is declared with `constraint:OnUpdate:CASCADE,onDelete:SET NULL` (`internal/models/groups.go:22`), so deleting the group also detaches every channel that was filed under it. The `DeletedAt` column is a plain `time.Time` rather than `gorm.DeletedAt`, so `DeleteRecordFromDb` issues a real `DELETE`, not a soft delete.

A second, smaller defect in the same handler: the `uuid.Parse(group_id)` error branch does not `return`, so a malformed group id still falls through to the delete call.

## Where

- Route: `pkg/router/group.go:30` - `organisationUrl.DELETE("/:org_id/groups/:group_id", group.DeleteGroup)` on the group created at line 19 with `middleware.Authorize` only.
- Controller: `pkg/controller/group/group.go:188-227` - parses both UUIDs and calls `group.DeleteGroup(base.Db, ids)`; `c.Get("userClaims")` is never called, so `user_id` and the caller's organisation are never consulted. Line 202-206: the invalid-group-id branch writes a 400 but does not `return`.
- Service: `services/group/group.go:80-97` - `org.CheckOrgExists(ids["organisation_id"], ...)` then `g.DeleteGroup(db, ids)`; there is no membership or role check.
- Model: `internal/models/groups.go:153-165` - `CheckExists(db, &g, "organisation_id = ? AND id = ?", ids["organisation_id"], ids["group_id"])` followed by a delete; both predicates come from the attacker-supplied URL.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in as any user and copy the access token.
2. Take a victim organisation id and one of its group ids (organisation ids appear in invite links and issue URLs; group ids are returned by `GET /organisations/:org_id/groups` to members).
3. Call:

   `curl -X DELETE "https://<host>/api/v1/organisations/<victim_org_id>/groups/<victim_group_id>" -H "Authorization: Bearer <attacker_token>"`

4. The response is `200` `"Group deleted successfully"` and the victim organisation's group is removed, with its channels detached from the group.

## Expected

- `403` or `404` unless the caller is a member/admin of the organisation in the path and has permission to delete groups.

## Actual

- `200` and the group is deleted for a caller with no relationship to the organisation.

## Suggested fix

- Read `userClaims` in the controller, verify the caller belongs to `org_id` (and is an org admin), and load the group scoped to that organisation before deleting.
- Add the missing `return` after the invalid `group_id` error response.

Source links: https://github.com/Zedu-Endor/zedu-be/blob/67db4db20f1876a644f6b305575303aa312c5ce0/pkg/router/group.go#L30 , https://github.com/Zedu-Endor/zedu-be/blob/67db4db20f1876a644f6b305575303aa312c5ce0/pkg/controller/group/group.go#L188 , https://github.com/Zedu-Endor/zedu-be/blob/67db4db20f1876a644f6b305575303aa312c5ce0/internal/models/groups.go#L153
